claims.text: Advanced or adaptive sampling can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The proposed scope includes elemental, binary, and multicomponent systems in both solid and fluid states near phase transitions.
Advanced sampling will reduce the computational cost of free-energy calculations.
The method is intended to operate at high temperatures near phase transitions.
The method will evaluate free energies for both solid and fluid states.
Enhanced sampling improves sampling efficiency in free-energy calculations.
The proposed method can retain vibrational-entropy contributions while reducing cost.
The proposed method can retain anharmonic contributions while reducing cost.
The proposed method can retain electron–vibration coupling while reducing cost.
The proposed method will increase throughput for fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic calculations.
The proposed method will have fidelity comparable to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method will have fidelity comparable to TOR-TILD.
A 1–2% tolerance against explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics and TOR-TILD results is proposed as the decisive fidelity threshold.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis targets high-entropy systems, but the stated boundary describes elemental and binary systems as included high-entropy systems. Elemental systems are not compositionally high-entropy, and binary systems are not generally classified as high-entropy systems without further qualification.
